detail.longDescription: I’m curious how people manage their SSH keys if you use multiple devices like your home or work triple boot desktop, dual boot travel laptop, the test box that gets wiped three times a week and so on? I figured I’m not the only one with this problem. Right now, I’m keeping them in a repo (hosted on my home network, no outside connectivity - I know better than to put something this important on GitHub et al) with the configuration. This feels suboptimal, but at least not much worse than having a separate set of keys for every machine. I already use # KeePassXC so importing the private keys into it may make things a bit more secure. What do you do to (mostly) safely manage your SSH keys for your personal # selfhosted setups? I’m not talking about corporate security levels here, but maybe just one more layer on top of encrypted volumes that are already in place. # CyberSecurity # security # HomeLab
